title: Distilling Multimodal Biomedical Foundation Models for Edge Tuberculosis Screening: Client-Side WebAssembly Deployment and Conformal Clinical Abstention
content: Background: Deep learning for tuberculosis triage risks shortcut learning and overconfidence. We evaluate distilling BioMedCLIP into an edge-deployable architecture with a selective conformal safety interlock. Methods: A DenseNet-121 student (7.74M parameters) was trained on 12,599 radiographs via Tri-Loss distillation from a frozen BioMedCLIP teacher (86.4M parameters). Validation evaluated 3,441 radiographs: a primary within-scanner clinical benchmark (Combined India: Solan N=155, NITRD N=278) and an adversarial compression stress-test (Pakistan N=3,008). Mondrian split-conformal prediction calibrated a three-tiered interlock: urgent molecular testing, autonomous clearance, and clinical referral. Findings: Distillation significantly outperformed the supervised baseline: Solan AUROC 0.9449 vs 0.8613; NITRD AUROC 0.9520 vs 0.8718; Combined India AUROC 0.9497 vs 0.8635; and Pakistan AUROC 0.8624 vs 0.4990 (all p < 0.0001). In Indian hospital cohorts, the system referred 63.1% of ambiguous active TB cases to clinicians, flagging 32.5% as urgent for GeneXpert testing, while autonomously clearing 77.4% of healthy controls (178/230). Against total screening volume (3,441 external scans), the interlock achieved an unconditional false-clearance rate of 0.26% (9/3,441; 0.00% on cavitary MDR-TB development proxy). Among confirmed active TB cases, the false-negative discharge rate was 4.4% in India (9/203, down from 16.3% on baseline) and 0.0% in Pakistan (0/2,494), counterbalanced by 63.1% clinical referral. Pure graph execution latency of the 27.0 MB WebAssembly model was 77.5 ms on reference x86_64 CPU. Interpretation: Distilling foundation models into selective classification networks reconciles diagnostic accuracy with edge efficiency. Rather than forcing uncalibrated decisions, the system clears normal scans, expedites molecular assays for high-confidence TB, and safely refers diagnostic ambiguity to clinicians. Funding: Independent departmental resources; no external commercial funding.
